chunks: A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Abi Abdillah, from Abu al-Khazraj al-Ansari, from Ali ibn Ghurab, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

The Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'Accursed, accursed is the one who throws his burden upon the people! Accursed, accursed is the one who wastes those whom he provides for.'

key_terms.كَلَّهُ: Burden/dependents — refers to the financial responsibility for oneself and one's dependents; one who throws this burden on others abandons self-reliance
key_terms.مَلْعُونٌ: Accursed/Damned — one upon whom the divine curse (la'na) has fallen, indicating severe moral and spiritual condemnation
key_terms.يَعُولُ: To provide for/support — the obligatory financial maintenance (nafaqa) owed to one's dependents such as wife, children, and parents

ai.seo_question: What did the Prophet Muhammad say about abandoning one's financial responsibilities to family?
ai.summary: In this hadith, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) reports a double condemnation from the Prophet Muhammad (SAWW) directed at two kinds of irresponsible behavior regarding financial obligations. The first curse targets a person who neglects his own self-sufficiency and becomes a burden on the community, while the second condemns one who fails to financially support those who depend on him. The repetition of 'accursed' twice for each offense emphasizes the severity of both forms of negligence in Islamic social ethics.
